key_insight: Efficient wrapper-based feature selection can improve wind and solar power forecasting by identifying the most informative inputs without relying on unnecessary variables. The paper combines evidence from structured literature reviews and empirical analysis to show that better feature selection can make renewable energy prediction more accurate and practical.
problem_solved: Renewable energy output is highly variable because it depends on weather and environmental conditions, making accurate prediction difficult. The paper addresses how to improve forecasting performance while keeping models efficient and robust.
method: Conducted two structured literature reviews focused on real-world wind and solar power prediction studies.
Evaluated wrapper-based feature selection methods to identify the most predictive input features.
Compared forecasting performance and efficiency to understand where feature selection adds the most value.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights a practical way to boost prediction quality in energy systems while reducing model complexity. It is especially useful for applications where interpretability, efficiency, and operational reliability matter.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing data inputs, feature selection, and forecast output
Before-vs-after comparison chart of model performance with and without feature selection
Icon set for wind turbines, solar panels, weather variables, and prediction accuracy
Flowchart summarizing the literature review and empirical evaluation process
paper_title: Improving Wind and Solar Power Prediction with Efficient Wrapper-based Feature Selection: An Empirical Study
paper_authors: Daniel Grillmeyer, Marius Hadry, Michael Stenger, Vanessa Borst, Veronika Lesch
